      About

      I build systems that keep data flowing and production stable—backend services, pipelines, and automation that turn messy signals into reliable outcomes. Over 6+ years, I’ve shipped anomaly detection + auto-remediation that cut incident rates 60% and improved MTTR 40%, while owning SLA-critical workflows end to end.

      My recent work also spans ranking/retrieval + low-latency search (Python/SQL jobs, indexing workflows, feature refresh, Azure AI Search), with a strong bias for measurable impact and clean engineering: monitoring, tests, debugging, and clear system design.

      Top skills

      Python (Programming Language) • Statistical Data Analysis • SQL • Product Management • Problem Solving

      • Post

        Some moments stop you in your tracks.
        Receiving the Graduate Student Leadership Award from the University of San Francisco is one of those moments for me. The kind that makes you look back at the road that brought you here and feel an overwhelming sense of gratitude for every single person who walked it with you. This isn't just my award. It belongs to every person who helped shape who I am.

        To my parents, you worked tirelessly, sacrificed quietly, and never once let me doubt that I could reach further than you did. Everything I stand on, I built on your shoulders. Thank you for being my foundation.

        To all my teachers and mentors, your patience outlasted my confusion, your belief in me outlasted my self-doubt, and your wisdom showed up exactly when I needed it most. You didn't just teach me, you shaped how I think, lead, and show up for others.

        To everyone who gave me the opportunity to serve, thank you for trusting me with your time, your communities, and your goals. Leadership only means something when people choose to walk alongside you, and you did.

        To the University of San Francisco, thank you for creating an environment where students are challenged to grow not just academically, but as human beings and as leaders. Proud to be a Don!

        And to my family and friends and everyone who believed in me, sometimes louder than I believed in myself, I hope I can pay that forward!

        #USF #GraduateStudentLeadership #Grateful #MSInformationSystems #Blessed

        I am thrilled to share that I’ve earned the Project Management Professional (PMP)® certification from the Project Management Institute!

        The journey sharpened how I can:
        •Turn ambiguity into outcome-driven roadmaps with clear acceptance criteria and incremental delivery
        •Estimate responsibly (ranges, confidence), visualize flow, and make trade-offs transparent
        •Build quality in: definition of done, peer reviews, automated checks, and repeatable releases
        •Balance predictive planning with adaptive execution—using the right mix of iterative cadences and stage-gates
        •Keep stakeholders aligned with crisp comms, visible risk registers, and data-backed decisions
        •Use core tools well: WBS & network diagrams for scheduling, EVM for performance, and lightweight dashboards for throughput and stability
        •Foster healthy teams: servant leadership, blameless reviews, and fast feedback loops that actually improve the next iteration

        Grateful for everyone who shared time, code reviews, and war stories. Can’t wait to apply these habits to initiatives that matter. 🚀 Excited to apply this milestone to drive impactful projects ahead.

        #PMP #ProjectManagement #PMI #ProfessionalGrowth

        I am thrilled to share that our team, Pulse Point, won the Organizational Impact Award at the finals of the PMI Next Generation Leaders (NGL) Program!

        The program, inspired by PMI’s vision of “inspiring youth to achieve their goals, making dreams a reality,” has been an incredible journey of experiential learning, collaboration, and growth. Competing with multiple teams, we had the opportunity to work on impactful business cases and create value for the PMI NGL program—and it’s truly humbling that our efforts were recognized.

        A huge thank you to the leadership team—        Dhruti Joshi, Shelby Austin, CSM, PMP, Sugitha Kamaraj, and our mentor, Kelvin Yip, for his constant guidance and support throughout this journey. Your insights and encouragement have been invaluable for us as a team.

        To my amazing team members Derek Huynh and Patrick Tarumbwa—this win belongs to all of us.

        With my team’s support, I learned so much transitioning into a product owner role, learning to communicate a clear vision, prioritize impact, collaborate, and adapt to changes.

        Being part of this program has not only strengthened my project management and leadership skills but also given me the opportunity to connect with passionate professionals who are ready to make a difference.
        I am excited for what lies ahead and to continue this journey of growth and impact!

        #PMI #NextGenerationLeaders #ProjectManagement #Leadership #Teamwork

        6mo •

        We are back! 👏 💡

        Episode 3, "The Long Game of Success with Prof.         Alessandra Cassar", of our podcast "She Means Business" is live now! 💡 👏 Check it out here! https://lnkd.in/g99iaEVt

        In the latest episode we talk about why traditional definitions of competitiveness fail to capture how women succeed. Drawing from experimental economics, biology, and workplace research, Prof. Cassar unpacks how cooperation, team-based leadership, and long-term strategies have shaped women’s success across history, and why modern organizations still reward male-coded behaviors.

        From negotiating promotions to leading teams and using AI as a potential equalizer, this conversation offers an empowering lens on success for women who want to compete without becoming someone they’re not.

        A big thank you to Afreen for leading this interview, Sopiko for making the connection and all the wonderful women behind the scenes at GWIB who show up and make this happen! 👏

        As I step into a new year, I’m filled with gratitude because I’m different from who I was when I arrived at USF in 2024.
        Starting my master’s in information systems at the University of San Francisco was a big leap. Like many international students, I came in with excitement and uncertainty, a new country, new routines, and pressure to figure everything out fast. Over time, USF became more than a campus, it became home.
        Being part of the MSIS Class of 2025 has been one of the most meaningful chapters of my life. I earned my master’s degree, learned so much inside and outside the classroom, and found myself becoming more confident, not just in my skills, but also in my voice.
        An experience I’ll always hold close is serving as a teaching assistant for multiple subjects. It pushed me to learn more, build patience, and support others. I’m especially thankful to         Eric C. Lacy, MSc. IS for this opportunity, the experience shaped me in ways I didn’t expect.
        I also want to thank Kourosh Dadgar, PhD, PMP for being a steady source of guidance throughout my journey. Whenever I felt stuck or unsure, you helped make things manageable. Thank you for answering my questions and leading the MSIS program with so much care.
        A big part of my heart at USF has been the international student community. I’m grateful to International Student and Scholar Services for the chance to be an International Student Guide during orientation week, meeting students from so many places, helping them settle in, and being the person I wish I had met when I first arrived. I was honored to receive the International Service Pin Award for serving the international student community. I’m proud of it because it represents something personal: showing up for others when you know what it feels like to be new.
        I’m also humbled to share that I was selected as the Fall 2025 recipient of the Dean’s Medal of Excellence from the Masagung Graduate School of Management, recognizing leadership, academic excellence, and alignment with the university’s mission and values. It means a lot because it reflects what I cared most about at USF, being involved, supporting students, creating inclusive spaces, and contributing wherever I could.
        To my classmates, thankyou for the perspectives, teamwork, and friendships, you made this journey richer. To the communities and clubs I found along the way, especially the University of San Francisco SOM Graduate Student Board and Graduate Women In Business Club thank you for letting me help build events and spaces that made student life better.
        To my family and friends, your support and encouragement gave me the confidence and faith I needed to pursue this dream, even on the days it felt hard.
        USF’s motto, "Change the world from here", used to mean these classrooms. Now “here” feels bigger, it’s the communities we build and the people we uplift, wherever we stand next!
        I'm grateful for past years, & entering this new year with the lessons, people, and memories with me!

        Attending the Grace Hopper Celebration for the first time as a new grad and early-career professional was nothing short of transformative. I arrived hopeful, but I left inspired, grounded, and deeply grateful.
        My biggest “wow” moment came during the keynote by the         AnitaB.org CEO Brenda Darden Wilkerson. She spoke about how the land beneath our feet can feel like shifting sand in today’s rapidly changing tech landscape. Her analogy of the Sahara Desert feeding the Amazon ecosystems was a powerful reminder that unexpected connections and contributions help entire communities thrive. It perfectly captured this year’s theme: unbound.

        I was also grateful to host and be part of several Braindates throughout the conference, spaces filled with curiosity, openness, and thoughtful dialogue.

        Beyond sessions and events, the people truly made GHC25 unforgettable. I had the chance to meet Ala Stolpnik from Wisary, an AI coaching platform built to help you think like a product leader. Their approach really stood out to me, helping turn early ideas into clear, purposeful plans by connecting business goals, user needs, and technical decisions with thoughtful guidance. Seeing how intentionally they’re shaping AI to support product managers, rather than replace them, was both energizing and unique.

        Being in Chicago surrounded by thousands of women and allies, students, engineers, founders, researchers, and leaders, it felt like stepping into an ecosystem built on generosity and shared purpose. As someone early in my career, connecting with so many like-minded, mission-driven individuals made me feel both supported and unbound in what’s possible.
        Walking away from GHC2025, I feel renewed, motivated, and committed to contributing to this community that uplifts, innovates, and leads with intention.

        #GHC2025 #GraceHopperCelebration #WomenInTech #AnitaBOrg

        GHC 2025 — more than a conference, it’s momentum. 🌟

        I’m thrilled to be heading to the Grace Hopper Celebration this fall—the world’s largest gathering of women and non-binary technologists. For me, GHC is where ideas turn into action and inclusion meets real engineering: a space to learn, grow, and build alongside people reimagining what’s possible.

        This year, I’m excited to build on my recent GenAI panels (USF and ATXpo @ San José State) by hosting two Braindates:

        • GenAI ≠ Consent: Ethical Limits on AI Access to Public Web Data—how to build responsibly without slowing delivery.
        • GenAI Literacy: What Colleges Teach and Workplaces Need—bridging coursework to shipping code.

        I bring 6 years building reliable, data-driven systems (Python, SQL, AWS), automation that drove ~60% fewer incidents and ~40% faster MTTR, and end-to-end work across data pipelines, AI/ML prototypes, and decision-ready dashboards. I’m exploring Data Engineer, Data Analyst, and Product (PM/APM/Product Analyst) roles for 2026—and I’d love to connect with engineers, students, and recruiters who care about reliability, data platforms, and responsible AI.

        👉 Portfolio:         https://lnkd.in/dPwBVbnD

        Here’s to bold ideas, new connections, and meaningful impact at #GHC25. 💙
